raw_response:
I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. I have about 12 mu total. There is no question what I will grow — wheat in winter, corn in summer, same as everyone in my village. That rotation works on this flat ground with our water. I know how to do it, I know what inputs to buy at the supply shop in town, and the grain traders come here to buy. Why would I try something different at my age?

For the wheat, I plant in mid-October after the corn comes off. I use the improved seed from the county supply cooperative — I do not save my own seed anymore, the shop seed yields better. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea in spring. I irrigate four times: before winter freeze, when it greens up, at jointing, and at grain-filling. I spray herbicide in early spring and fungicide before heading. I use the rotary tiller to work the maize stubble under before planting.

For the corn, I plant right after the wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed — always hybrid, everyone does. I direct-seed into the stubble now, no plowing, it saves time and the machine hire is cheap. Summer rains usually carry the crop but I irrigate once if it gets dry. I put on fertilizer twice: at planting and when the plant is knee-high.
